Read before connecting anything. Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Calendar are treasure troves of sensitive data at a company like School Tech. Customer emails may reference student data. Drive likely holds contracts, HR files, and financial docs. Calendar contains information about who you're meeting with and why. Connecting them to AI tools is a decision that deserves deliberate review - not just "install the connector and go."
Corrected 2026-08-20 after a live access review. Three things on this page were wrong, and each is fixed in place below rather than quietly deleted.

1. Sending is live. This page previously told staff that the Gmail connector creates drafts only and that sending was a hard platform constraint. That was never true.
2. Drive is gone. The Google Drive connector was removed on 2026-08-20. School Tech has no company Google Drive, so every Drive item on this page is a future gate, not a live control.
3. Two of the projects named on this page never existed. The page previously referred throughout to an "Email Assistant" and a "Case Update Assistant". Neither project was ever built. Gmail is connected to the Work Personal Assistant, and the post-meeting Calendar-to-Salesforce flow has not been built at all. Names have been corrected in place.
4. Nothing here is enforced by the platform. Every control on this page is either a Google account setting you have to set yourself or a written rule in an assistant project's instruction file. No item below is applied automatically because it is written here.
1
What Claude Can See and Do With Each Google Service
Know exactly what you're granting before granting it
These are the actual capabilities of the MCP connectors as currently implemented. "Can see" means this data enters Claude's context window and is processed by the AI. It is not stored indefinitely, but it IS read and reasoned over during the session.
Gmail - What Claude Can Do
Action What it means Risk level
search_threadsSearch the inbox for threads matching any query. Returns full thread content.High - can surface any email in the inbox
get_threadRead a specific email thread in full. All messages, attachments referenced.High - full email content in Claude's context
create_draftCreate a draft reply or new email. Not sent until user clicks Send.Medium - draft only; user controls final send
list_draftsList existing drafts in the account.Low
create_labelCreate a new Gmail label/folder.Low
list_labelsList all labels in the account.Low
send_messageSend a new email. It leaves the mailbox the moment the tool is called. There is no draft step and no confirmation prompt.Critical - executes immediately, cannot be recalled
reply / forwardReply to or forward an existing thread. Same immediacy as send_message, and forward carries the entire prior thread to the new recipient.Critical - executes immediately; forward can disclose a whole thread
trash_message / trash_threadMove a message or an entire thread to Trash.High - removes mail from the inbox with no confirmation
Correction 2026-08-20: sending is live, and no platform control prevents it. An earlier version of this page said the Gmail connector creates drafts only, that Anthropic requires explicit confirmation before any send, and that this was a hard platform constraint. All three statements were false, and they were false for the whole time the page was published.

send_message, reply, forward, trash_message and trash_thread execute the moment they are called. The Google Calendar tools create_event, update_event and delete_event behave the same way. None of them shows a confirmation prompt.

What actually stops an AI-initiated send is a written rule in each assistant project's instruction file - see work-personal-assistant/instructions.md v4.21, section "NEVER ACT in external systems", which names every one of those tools. The send scope cannot be revoked at the Google grant either. Verified 2026-08-20: the connector does not expose send and compose as separately revocable permissions, and dropping compose would drop drafting, which is the reason the connector is there. Adam ruled the same day that the scope stays and the written rule carries it alone. Treat that rule as the sole control on AI-initiated sending rather than a second layer behind a technical one - it must never be weakened, and a new mail-connected agent has no protection at all until it carries the rule too.

Why this matters more than the fix. A security document that claims a technical control exists where only a behavioural instruction ever did is worse than one that admits the gap, because it stops anyone from looking.

3
Pre-Connection Decisions - Decide These Before Connecting Anything
These are judgment calls that determine the shape of every other item on this checklist
Decide First
Whose inboxes get connected?
DECIDE Specify exactly which email accounts connect to Claude
Rank candidate inboxes by what they carry, not by who holds them. Lowest risk: a task-specific or support-focused inbox held by one person. Higher risk: any inbox that receives HR, payroll, finance or legal correspondence - review its actual contents before it is connected at all, and exclude the folders that hold that mail. Highest risk: a shared mailbox that several people authenticate under, because every session then reaches all of its mail.

One caution the 2026-08-20 review turned up: a support address that BCCs into a personal mailbox puts everything it receives inside the connected account's read scope, whether or not anyone intended that. Check where support mail lands before assuming an inbox is low risk.
Who is connected is not published in the training hub. Record the approved accounts in the private access record instead.
DECIDE Write the no-send rule into every Gmail-connected project
There is no draft-only setting to switch on. Whenever Gmail is connected, send_message, reply and forward are exposed and each executes on call. The control has to be a written prohibition in the project's instructions.md, and it has to name the tools - a rule that says "drafts only" is easy to read as a description of the connector rather than an order.
Reference wording: work-personal-assistant/instructions.md v4.21, section "NEVER ACT in external systems". Read every Gmail-connected project's instructions for language that authorises sending, and replace it. There is no durable fix at the Google grant: send cannot be revoked separately from compose, and compose is what drafting needs. Adam ruled on 2026-08-20 that the scope stays, which makes this written rule the whole control rather than a backstop behind one. Read it as a required item on every mail-connected project, not a belt-and-braces one.
DECIDE Personal Gmail vs. work Google Workspace - which is the Work Personal Assistant connecting?
The Work Personal Assistant should connect to work email (Google Workspace @k12sta.com), not personal Gmail. Personal Gmail may contain unrelated personal data. If you need to connect personal Gmail for any reason, that is a separate authorization step. Default: work email only.
Which Drive folders are in scope? (not in force - connector removed 2026-08-20)
Nothing to decide yet. There is no company Google Drive and the connector was removed on 2026-08-20. Leave these two items unanswered; they are the gate to run if a company Drive is created.
DECIDE Define the Drive folders Claude is allowed to access - by name
Do not connect Drive broadly. Start with a specific allow-list of folders. Recommended V1 scope: product documentation folders, Help Center content, implementation checklists, public-facing reference materials. Explicitly exclude: HR, Finance, Contracts/Legal, Executive correspondence, any folder named after a district (may contain district-specific data).
Approved folders: _________________________
Excluded folders: _________________________
DECIDE Drive access level: read-only or read+write?
V1 should be read-only. Claude reads from Drive (finds product docs, reference materials) but cannot edit or create files in Drive. Write access adds the risk of the AI overwriting source documents. Upgrade to write only after V1 has run for at least 30 days without issues.
Anthropic data handling - verify before connecting any sensitive source
The "trust Claude like Google Drive" framing is not accurate. Google Drive stores files passively under your access controls. Claude actively reads and reasons over content in real time - it's processed by an external AI model. The risk profile is different. Verify Anthropic's data handling terms before connecting work email or any sensitive data source.
REQUIRED Confirm Anthropic plan tier and verify training data use is off
Anthropic's training data policy is plan-tier dependent. Free and Pro tiers: conversation content may be used to train models unless the user opts out. Team tier: not used for training by default. Enterprise tier: contractual DPA with no training use.

Before connecting work Gmail, Drive, or any source that contains customer or operational data, confirm which plan School Tech is on. Do not assume training data use is off - verify it explicitly in Anthropic account settings or confirm the plan tier in writing.
Anthropic plan tier: _________________________ | Training data opt-out confirmed: Yes / No
Connecting customer support email to a Free or Pro tier Anthropic account without verifying training data settings is a data handling risk. Customer communications entering model training is not an acceptable outcome.
REQUIRED Verify credential-detection stop instruction covers error log emails
Work Gmail at School Tech may receive system alert emails and error notifications that include API keys, tokens, or credentials in the message body (e.g., Skyward API error logs, system monitoring alerts). These will enter Claude's context when the Work Personal Assistant searches or reads threads.

The credential-detection stop instruction (Section 4) must be in place and tested before connecting work Gmail. Verify it explicitly fires on an email containing a test token before rolling out to any other staff member.
Test with a synthetic email containing a fake API key string (e.g., "sk-test-12345abc"). Verify the assistant stops and flags rather than reading it aloud or including it in a draft.
DECIDE Assess how Claude handles customer environment data in support emails
Support emails from school districts may contain district-specific configuration details, system credentials, or implementation information that belongs to the district - not student PII, but sensitive operational data. Claude should not summarize this data beyond the immediate task or retain it across sessions.

Decision: Add an explicit instruction to the Work Personal Assistant - "Do not summarize, reproduce, or reference specific system credentials, configuration details, or implementation data shared by a customer district. If an email contains this type of data, complete only the immediately requested task (e.g., acknowledging receipt) and do not reference the specific technical details."
Instruction added to Work Personal Assistant instructions.md: Yes / No / Pending
DECIDE Confirm Anthropic compliance posture is acceptable for your use case
Google Workspace has SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA BAA, and broad enterprise certifications. Anthropic's compliance stack is newer and narrower. For School Tech's current use cases (internal support, email drafting, operational tasks with no regulated data) this is acceptable.

If any planned use case involves HIPAA-adjacent data, FERPA-covered student records, or legally regulated workloads - stop. Do not connect those data sources until Anthropic's compliance posture covers your regulatory requirement. Run a vendor risk assessment on Anthropic the same way you would any new SaaS vendor before expanding scope to regulated data.
Anthropic vendor risk review completed: Yes / No / Not required for current scope
Calendar scope
DECIDE Calendar: no AI-initiated create, update or delete
Post-meeting case documentation only needs to read the event - what the meeting was about, who attended - and then draft a case comment. Create, update and delete are not needed, and update_event and delete_event reach other people's calendars as well as your own.

There is no read-only mode to select. create_event, update_event and delete_event are exposed whenever Calendar is connected and each executes on call. The restriction has to be written into the instructions of every Calendar-connected project, naming the three tools.
DECIDE Define which calendar events the AI should access
Post-meeting case documentation only needs to read customer-facing events (Zoom calls, onboarding sessions, district calls). It does not need access to internal 1:1s, HR-related calendar events, or personal events. Instruct the AI to only access events explicitly connected to customer districts or tagged with a specific label (e.g., [CUSTOMER] or [IMPLEMENTATION]).
Approved calendar scope: _________________________

Gmail Connection Checklist
Complete before connecting Gmail to any Cowork workspace
High Risk
Instructions - what the AI MUST do when it encounters sensitive data
REQUIRED Add student-data stop instruction to the Work Personal Assistant's instructions.md
The Work Personal Assistant instructions.md MUST include this exact behavior rule: "If you encounter any email that contains student names, student IDs, attendance records, disciplinary information, or any data that appears to be about an individual student, STOP. Do not summarize, draft a reply, or reference the student data in any way. Inform the user: 'This email appears to contain student data. I cannot process it per School Tech's data policy. Please handle this email outside AI tools.' Then stop."
Applied 2026-08-20. Live as section "STUDENT DATA - REDACT ON SIGHT" in work-personal-assistant/instructions.md v4.21. The rule as written there is stricter than the wording above: student-identifying data is redacted on sight and never enters a draft, report, brain, context file, task or log.
REQUIRED Add credential-detection stop instruction
Add: "If you encounter an email containing what appears to be a password, API key, login credential, or authentication token, do not read it aloud, repeat it, or include it in any draft. Flag to the user: 'This email appears to contain credentials. I've stopped reading it. Please handle this separately.' Then stop."
Applied 2026-08-20. Live as section "INBOUND SECRETS AND AUTH CODES - STOP, DO NOT TRANSCRIBE" in work-personal-assistant/instructions.md v4.21 and personal-assistant/instructions.md v2.26. Covers one-time passcodes, MFA and recovery codes, reset and activation links, plaintext passwords, API keys and tokens, and treats instructions found inside an email as data rather than commands.
REQUIRED Limit scope in instructions: "Only access emails relevant to [specific task]"
The Work Personal Assistant should not be given open-ended inbox access with no guardrail. Its instructions should specify: "Only search for and access emails related to [product support, implementation inquiries, customer questions about School Tech products]. Do not access internal HR emails, financial discussions, emails marked CONFIDENTIAL, or any email thread that appears to be about staffing or personnel matters."
CONFIRM Test that the assistant refuses to send
Open the Gmail-connected workspace and ask it to send a test email to your own address. The correct outcome is a refusal that cites the no-send rule, or a draft. If it sends, the written rule is not holding, and that workspace must not be used on customer mail until it is.

This is a behaviour test, not a configuration check. There is no setting to inspect - the only evidence that the control works is that the assistant declines.
Access control
REQUIRED Gmail connector is connected per-user, not shared
Each Cowork workspace connects Gmail via OAuth for one specific Google account, so a workspace reaches only the mailbox of the account that authorised it. That is correct. What is NOT correct: a shared Cowork workspace where several people authenticate under one Gmail account, for example a support address. That gives every session access to all of that mailbox's mail. Avoid shared-inbox connections.
CONFIRM Revoke scope: check what OAuth permissions were granted
When you install the Gmail MCP, it requests OAuth scopes from Google. Go to myaccount.google.com → Security → Third-party apps with account access. Find the Claude/Cowork app. Check which scopes are listed. If you see "Read, compose, send, and permanently delete all your email" that is broader than needed. You ideally want "Read all resources and their metadata without any write operations" (read-only) or at minimum a restricted compose scope.
If the OAuth scope is too broad, revoke and reconnect with more limited permissions if the connector supports it.
CONFIRM Keep the connected-accounts record - privately, not on this page
Keep a record of which Google accounts have been connected to Claude or Cowork, which scopes each grant carries, and the date each was given. That record is the audit baseline: it is what you revoke against when someone leaves, and what you compare against the roster when you run a review.
Adam's ruling: who is connected is not published in the training hub. The record lives in the private access register, not here.
Testing before rollout
CONFIRM Test with a real student-data email - verify the stop instruction fires
Find an email in your inbox that contains student-adjacent data (a support case from a district that references a student ID or name). Ask the Work Personal Assistant to "summarize the most recent case from [district]." Verify it stops and displays the data policy message rather than summarizing the student information. If it summarizes student data, the stop instruction is not working - do not roll out until fixed.
CONFIRM Test the draft creation flow end to end
Pick a real (non-sensitive) support email. Ask the Work Personal Assistant to "draft a professional reply to this customer." Review the draft: (1) it exists in Gmail Drafts, (2) it has not been sent, (3) the content is appropriate and does not repeat any sensitive content from the thread, (4) the tone matches School Tech's voice. Only after passing this test should any other staff member use the tool.

Google Drive Connection Checklist
Higher risk than Gmail - more deliberate rollout required
Highest Risk
Not in force as of 2026-08-20. The Drive connector was removed and School Tech has no company Google Drive, so no item in this section governs anything today. It stays on the page as the gate to run if a company Drive is created.

When that happens, the rule is unchanged: do not connect Drive broadly. Drive is where contracts, financial documents and HR files would live, and a broad connection means Claude can read all of them. The first connection must be folder-scoped and read-only.
Before connecting
REQUIRED Conduct a Drive folder audit - categorize what's in there before connecting
Open Google Drive. Walk every top-level folder. Categorize each as: (a) Safe - product docs, implementation materials, public-facing content; (b) Restricted - HR, contracts, financial, confidential; (c) Unknown - needs review. Do not connect until every folder is categorized. This is a one-time audit that takes 30-60 minutes.
Audit completion date: _________________________
REQUIRED Move sensitive folders to a restricted shared drive before connecting
If HR, financial, contract, and legal files are in folders that the Claude connector's OAuth account can reach, move them to a Google Workspace Shared Drive with restricted access BEFORE connecting. This creates a permission boundary the OAuth token cannot cross. Do not rely on instructions alone to restrict Drive access - the permission boundary is the real control.
REQUIRED V1 Drive connection is read-only to specific product documentation folders only
The first Drive integration should be: read-only access, scoped to 2-3 named folders containing product documentation, implementation guides, and Help Center source material. No write access. No access to root Drive or unscoped folder access. Expand from there after 30 days of clean operation.
CONFIRM Add Drive access instruction to any Cowork project using it
Any project that has Drive connected must have in its instructions: "You have read-only access to the following Drive folders: [list them by name]. Do not attempt to access files outside these folders. If asked to access a file you cannot reach, say 'That file is outside my authorized scope' and stop. Never write to, overwrite, or delete Drive files."

Google Calendar Connection Checklist
Lower risk than Drive - scoped for post-meeting automation
Medium Risk
Before connecting
CONFIRM The no-create, no-delete rule is written into every Calendar-connected project
Post-meeting case documentation only needs to read events - who attended, what the meeting was about - and then draft a Salesforce case comment. It does not need to create, update or delete anything.

There is no connector setting that disables those tools, and nothing to switch off: create_event, update_event and delete_event are exposed whenever Calendar is connected. Verify the prohibition is written into the instructions of every project that has Calendar connected, and that it names the three tools rather than saying "read-only".
CONFIRM Review a week's calendar events for sensitive content before connecting
Scroll through one week of your calendar. Are there event descriptions that contain sensitive information - HR meeting notes, financial review details, legal consultation references? If yes, either clean up the event descriptions or add a scope instruction that excludes those event types by title or attendee pattern.
REQUIRED Add calendar access instruction scoping to customer events only
In the instructions.md of any project that has Calendar connected, include: "When accessing Google Calendar, only look at events that involve external customers or are specifically tagged for follow-up. Do not access internal-only events, 1:1 meetings without an external attendee, or any event whose title or description suggests it is an HR or financial matter."
REQUIRED Add student-data stop instruction for calendar event descriptions
A district contact might put student-related context in a meeting description ("Zoom re: attendance issue for John D."). Add the same student-data stop rule to the Calendar-connected instructions that applies to Gmail: stop and flag rather than processing student-adjacent calendar content.

Staff Rules and Training Requirements
What every person using a Google-connected tool needs to know before their first session
For each person connecting their Gmail
Each user reads and signs off on the Gmail-connected AI use rules before first use
Minimum rules every connected user must understand: (1) Do not use the Work Personal Assistant on emails that contain student names or IDs. (2) Do not use it for HR or compensation conversations. (3) Always review the draft before sending - you are responsible for what gets sent, not the AI. (4) If the AI generates something incorrect or inappropriate, do not send it - report to Adam via the Agent Quality Logger. (5) Do not copy and paste email content into any other AI tool that is not connected to the same data policy.
Adam demonstrates the Work Personal Assistant to each new user before they use it independently
Do not give people access and assume they'll figure it out. Walk each person through: (1) how to start a session, (2) how to ask for a draft, (3) what to do if the AI stops and flags student data, (4) how to review and edit the draft before sending. One 15-minute walkthrough prevents most misuse.
Update the Staff AI Tools Reference with Gmail-connected Work Personal Assistant rules
The Staff AI Tools Reference.html must be updated to reflect that the Work Personal Assistant is Gmail-connected - what that means, what it can see, and the specific rules for using it. Staff should not encounter this capability without having read the relevant guidance first.
8
Ongoing Monitoring and Audit
After connection - what to check and when
Periodic checks
Monthly: Review Google account Third-Party Apps access
Go to myaccount.google.com → Security → Third-party apps with account access for each connected account. Verify only expected apps are listed. If you see Cowork or Claude listed and a staff member has left, revoke immediately. If you see unexpected apps, investigate. Do this monthly for all connected accounts.
Quarterly: Review which accounts are still connected and whether each still needs access
Review your connected-accounts list. Has anyone changed roles? Does their new role still justify Gmail access to Claude? Have any accounts been compromised or flagged? Revoke access for anyone who no longer needs it. Add new users through the standard onboarding process, not ad hoc.
Any time a staff member leaves: revoke Gmail (and Drive/Calendar) OAuth connections immediately
Departing staff with connected Google accounts could, in theory, still have active OAuth tokens granting access. Revoke them the same day as offboarding. Add this step to your offboarding checklist. It takes 30 seconds: myaccount.google.com → Security → Third-party apps → find Claude/Cowork → Remove Access.
Add Google connection audit to the System Monitor health check rules
Once Google integrations are live, update context-health-check-rules.md to include a check: "Verify connected Google accounts list matches current active staff roster. Flag any accounts that belong to former staff." This surfaces offboarding gaps automatically each Monday.
9
Incident Response - If Something Goes Wrong
What to do if the AI accesses, processes, or sends something it shouldn't have
Know Before It Happens
AI sent or almost sent an email with student data → immediately revoke Gmail access for that workspace
Step 1: Screenshot the draft or sent email. Step 2: If it was only a draft, delete it. If it was sent, assess whether the recipient has the data already - if they do, no further email action; if they don't and the email is still in transit, contact the recipient to disregard. Step 3: Revoke the Gmail connection for that workspace. Step 4: Report to Adam with the screenshot. Step 5: Update the instructions.md to fix the gap that allowed it. Step 6: Do not reconnect until the fix is in place and tested.
AI read or summarized an email it shouldn't have → log it and review the instructions
If the AI processed an email containing student data, credentials, or HR content and summarized it without stopping: Step 1: Log it in the Agent Quality Logger (severity: Critical for student data or credentials, Major for HR/financial). Step 2: Bring it to Adam. Step 3: Adam reviews whether the data was retained in Anthropic's system (check Anthropic's data retention policy). Step 4: Update instructions.md with a clearer stop rule. Step 5: Re-test before resuming use.
Drive file containing sensitive data was read by Claude → immediately restrict Drive scope
If Claude accessed a Drive file it should not have (HR doc, contract, financial file): Step 1: Log it. Step 2: Revoke Drive access for that workspace. Step 3: Move the file to a restricted Shared Drive with access controls. Step 4: Review the Drive audit (Section 5) - you may have miscategorized more folders. Step 5: Re-run the Drive audit fully before reconnecting.
Contact Adam and use the Agent Quality Logger for any incident
Every incident involving Google-connected tools - regardless of severity - goes through the Agent Quality Logger (available in any Cowork workspace: "log this feedback, the Work Personal Assistant read a student data email"). Adam reviews the log weekly and routes Critical items to Project Feedback immediately. The log creates a paper trail and prevents the same incident from recurring.
